protocol.operation: Fresh counted callback and initial user-state/core solver construction; full core MIGRAD (C++ VariableMetricMinimizer::Minimize vs Julia migrad); owned parameter vector, error vector and full row-major covariance materialization; fval, EDM, NFcn, actual callback count, validity, covariance and termination flags. Five unbounded cases: internal parameters equal external parameters. Excludes immutable Gaussian input parsing/preparation, optional global correlation coefficients, JSON serialization. The retained initial Julia samples use BenchmarkTools with gctrial=true, gcsample=false and overhead=0. Fixed-duration blocks use Julia time_ns and C++ steady_clock around one complete operation, with no forced GC between blocks.
protocol.mandatory: Both valid; all required outputs finite; required covariance present; no missing rows; same per-process output across all warmed samples; exact callback counts within each implementation. Strict parity failures retained; Rosenbrock diagnostic pass does not authorize equivalent-computation speed claim.
protocol.uncertainty: Report paired median ratios and their observed range. Each process contributes the median of its declared timing-block medians. Require the declared per-language block-spread and paired-ratio-spread limits over every retained block and process. These are descriptive finite-experiment limits, not population confidence intervals or universal speed claims.

timing_reliability.timed_clock: Julia time_ns / C++ steady_clock; same owned-output operation boundaries
timing_reliability.admission: Strict numerical agreement, same-language output identity across processes, per-language block spread, and paired-ratio spread must all pass; retain failures.
